Testimony of Kathleen D. Moneghan, President, Maine Academy of Physician Associates In Support of
LD 651 "An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Program"
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and members of the Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, my name is Kathleen Moneghan. I am the President of the Maine Academy of Physician Associates (MEAPA), a Dover-Foxcroft resident, and I practice medicine in Occupational Health and Urgent Care. MEAPA is a non-profit organization that represents PAs practicing in Maine, providing care for Mainers. Today, I am testifying on behalf of MEAPA in support of LD 651 "An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Program." In 2020, LD 1660, "An Act to Increase Access to Physician Assistant Care," was signed into law to increase access to care throughout Maine where PAs frequently serve as primary care and emergency care providers in rural areas. This law ensures Maine PAs can practice at the full extent of their training, experience, and expertise, with optimal team practice.
Our state is familiar with the healthcare provider shortage that plagues Maine and the nation. There are over 1,000 PAs practicing in Maine, totaling just under 50% of the physician workforce. In Maine, 45% of PAs are hospital based, while 40% are outpatient/clinic based. On a federal level, PA workforce is growing exponentially; US News and World report consistently list the PA profession as a top 5 profession, with projected 28% profession expansion by the year 2031 (3). The intensity and efficiency of the PA training allows for a more rapid deployment, streamlining access to care issues.
PAs are Master's and increasingly Doctoral-level trained providers, accumulating several years of significant educational debt. According to the American Academy of Physician Associates, the average cost for a physician assistant program was $50,567 for an in-state resident and $61,088 for an out-of-state student. (2). The average student debt following PA school is $120K, which does not include undergraduate debt.
Maine has experienced many PAs seeking employment in other states due to the high burden of student loans. Many practices are experiencing increased attrition of providers due to the high cost of living and high student loan burden not commensurate with the ability to purchase homes and start families in Maine. Allocation of funds to lessen the significant burden of student loans will support health care providers already practicing in Maine and incentivize new Physician Associates who make up a substantial portion of the healthcare provider workforce, to work in Maine.
Thank you for your time and consideration,
Kathleen Moneghan, DHA, MPAS, PA-C President, Maine Academy of Physician Associates

Testimony ofRep. Kelly Noonan Murphy introducing
LD 651, An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment
Program
Before the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Senator Rafferty and distinguished colleagues of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and
Cultural Affairs, my name is Kelly Murphy, and I represent part of Scarborough. I am pleased to
sponsor LD 651, An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment
Program.

This bill would provide ongoing funding of $1 million annually for the program, which is administered by the Finance Authority of Maine (FAME).
The 130th Maine Legislature created the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Pilot
Program with $1 million in federal pandemic relief funding (ARPA and MJRP) and subsequently
has received state funding through state appropriations. The program is geared toward certain
health care professionals to address critical workforce shortages exacerbated by the COVID-19
pandemic, including, but not limited to, the behavioral health and oral care sectors. Under the
program, FAME pays up to $25,000 per year and, in aggregate, the lesser of $75,000 or 50% of
the recipient's outstanding loan balance.

The program is popular and competitive. There have been two award cycles resulting in the selection of 96 participants in the program. The third and most recent awards cycle opened on Feb. 1 and will close on March 31. It is expected that another 15 recipients will be chosen during this round. This third cycle will absorb the remaining program funds.

Maine is facing acute workforce shortages across health care fields. For example, the
Organization of Maine Nurse Leaders estimates that Maine lacked 2,115 registered nurses in 2024, and that number is expected to grow to 2,817 by 2030. The Maine Hospital Association estimates that its member hospitals need an additional 250 respiratory therapists to meet current
needs. A recent survey of behavioral health providers in Maine showed a 21% vacancy rate for
mental health clinician positions. And demographics will exacerbate these shortages in the
coming years. A recent Maine Department of Labor health care occupations report noted that
approximately 30% of Maine's current health care workforce is over the age of 55.

District 125: Part of Scarborough

The Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Pilot Program helps to address our critical health care workforce shortages and should continue. The $1 million in proposed ongoing funding would translate into approximately 15-18 awards annually. Program awards are based on the following factors: (1) access to health care for the population where the applicant practices or intends to practice, such as number of vacancies within a local provider system, timeliness of appointments and whether they or their employer accepts Medicaid; (2) monthly student debt obligation payment as a percentage of gross monthly income; (3) the need for specific health care practitioners in a given employment region; and (4) the workforce needs of Maine health
care providers.
Thank you for your consideration of the bill. I will be happy to answer any questions you have

Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and members of the Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, my name is Lisa Harvey-McPherson RN. I am submitting testimony on behalf of Northern Light Health and our member organizations in support of this bill. Northern Light Health member organizations include 10 hospitals located in southern, central, eastern and northern Maine, 8 nursing facilities, air and ground ambulance, behavioral health, addiction treatment, pharmacy, primary and specialty care practices and a state-wide home care and hospice program. Ninety three percent of Maine's population lives in the Northern Light Health service area. Northern Light Health is also proud to be one of Maine's largest employers with more than 10,000 employees statewide.
Northern Light Health member organizations recruit in the state and nationally to employ health care professionals to care for patients throughout the State of Maine. With labor shortages in a variety of health professions, loan repayment is an important recruitment tool and promoting the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Pilot Program to individuals we are recruiting and to our new hires is an important strategy for our recruiters.
The loan repayment program is highly competitive with the number of applications far exceeding the amount of funds available. This bill provides $1 million dollars in ongoing funds to support the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Program. Program loan recipients may receive awards totaling up to $25,000 per year or, in aggregate, the lesser of $75,000 or 50% of the recipient's outstanding loan balance.
The program places eligibility emphasis on several highly competitive health care professions from doctors and nurses to behavioral health professionals, professional therapists and heath care technicians. To be eligible for the program heath care professionals must:
� Be licensed and/or certified by the state of Maine as a medical, dental, or behavioral health practitioner or be a person with a professionally recognized medical, dental or behavioral health credential in the state of Maine
� Have qualifying outstanding education loans and submit evidence of outstanding educational loan debt
� Be employed full-time as an eligible health care provider as determined by FAME
� Not currently benefiting from a loan forgiveness program or loan repayment program administered by FAME or another entity (excluding federal incomedriven repayment plans and the Public Service Loan Forgiveness program)

Senator Rafferty, Representative Noonan Murphy, and members of the Education. and
Cultural Affairs Committee,
My name is Sally Weiss, and I am here today on behalf of the Maine Hospital Association to testify in support of LD 651.
First, I would like to thank Representative Murphy for introducing this critical legislation to sustain
an essential healthcare workforce program.
Maine hospitals, like many healthcare providers across the state, are facing a severe shortage of
healthcare professionals, including doctors, nurse practitioners, physician assistants, nurses,
licensed social workers, respiratory therapists, radiology technologists, and many others. In February 2025, the Maine Hospital Association (MHA) conducted a survey to assess current
workforce needs and project future requirements based on the age distribution of the existing workforce. The results are alarming: Maine hospitals are actively recruiting for 4,227 budgeted positions, comprising 3,090 full-time and 1,137 part-time roles. Additionally, nearly 5,600 healthcare workers in the state are 55 years or older. These figures highlight not only the immediate demand for healthcare professionals but also the significant gap that will need to be filled as these workers retire. Furthennore, Maine is projected to experience a 36.2% increase in residents aged 65 and older by
2030, roughly 400,000 individuals. As we know, older adults typically require healthcare services
two to three times more than younger individuals, which will further increase demand. Given these
projections, we must take immediate action to attract and retain healthcare professionals,
especially in rural and underserved communities, where recruitment challenges are even more
pronounced.

Many healthcare providers, particularly doctors, nurses, and mental health professionals, are ofien
hesitant to work in these rural or underserved areas due to the high cost of education and the relatively lower salaries offered in these regions, combined with some of the challenges in securing housing and childcare. Loan repayment programs are an effective way to incentivize healthcare workers to take positions in these areas by offering to pay off part or all of their student loans in exchange for a commitment to work in underserved communities for a specified period of time.
Loan repayment programs, such as the one proposed in LD 651, are one of many tools we can use
to address the healthcare workforce shortage in Maine. By doing so, we can ensure that all
communities in Maine continue to have access to care close to home.
For these reasons, the Maine Hospital Association strongly supports LD 651.
Thank you for your time and consideration.

Testimony of Sarah Calder, MaineHealth
In Support of LD 651, "An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan
Repayment Program" March 31, 2025
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy and distinguished members of the Joint Standing
Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs, I am Sarah Calder, Senior Government Affairs Director at MaineHealth, and I am here to testify in support of LD 651, "An Act to Fund the
Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Program."
MaineHealth is an integrated non-profit hospital system that provides the full continuum of
health care services to the residents of eleven counties in Maine and one in New Hampshire.
MaineHealth is also the state's largest private employer with over 24,000 care team members,
but, we are facing a workforce crisis that is significantly impacting access to care. We are
currently recruiting for nearly 2,500 positions, including 117 physicians and over 540 nurses.
In the face of these challenges, MaineHealth is working hard to recruit new care team members and retain the ones that we have, through investment in compensation, workforce development,
care team engagement, and attention to work-life balance. Those investments, including $324 million in wages for non-executives and non-physicians since 2021, are paying off. In fact,
MaineHealth's care team member turnover rate has improved in the past two and a half years from 18% in 2022 to 13.8% in 2024, which is substantially better than our comparison
benchmark range of 14-21%.
Despite this improvement, national estimates suggest that 3 out of 4 entrants into the job market over the next 10 years will need to enter the health care field to meet the needs of our rapidly
aging population. As the oldest state in the nation, we must look to creative policy solutions to
meet the increased workforce demands and ensure timely access to health care services. LD 651
adds much needed funding to the highly successful Health Care Provider Loan Repayment
Program, which is one tool Maine can use to recruit and retain health care workers by helping to relieve the financial burden of an advanced degree.
The health care system in Maine is becoming exceedingly fragile, which is evidenced by the recent hospital and service closures, as well as the hundreds of patients stuck in our hospitals every day waiting for the next appropriate level of care. The workforce crisis is contributing to
the unraveling of our system of care, and we urge the Legislature to support several critical
workforce related bills this Session, including LD 651, to help address our state's growing
workforce needs.
Thank you and I would be happy to answer any questions you may have.

Testimony by William Norbert Governmental Affairs and Communications Manager
in Support of L.D. 651
An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Program
March 31, 2025
Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs
Senator Rafferty, Representative Murphy, and Distinguished Members of the Joint Standing Committee on Education and Cultural Affairs:
My name is Bill Norbert. I am the Governmental Affairs and Communications
Manager at the Finance Authority of Maine (FAME). I am here to testify in support of L.D. 651, An Act to Fund the Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Program.
FAME would like to thank Representative Murphy for sponsoring this bill to
provide meaningful, ongoing funding of $l million annually fora program we have had
the pleasure of administering since 2021.
The Maine Health Care Provider Loan Repayment Pilot Program was created by
the 130"` Maine Legislature with $1 million in federal pandemic funding (ARPA and
MJRP). It subsequently has received state funding through appropriations. The program
is geared toward certain health care professionals to address critical workforce shortages
exacerbated by the COVID-19 pandemic, including, but not limited to, the behavioral
health and oral care sectors. Under the program, FAME will pay up to $25,000 per year
and, in aggregate, the lesser of $75,000 and 50% of the recipient's outstanding loan
balance beginning in November 2023.
The program has proven to be popular and competitive. The first award cycle took place in October of 2022 and resulted in the selection of 18 eligible recipients from a pool of 1,021 applications. The second award cycle occurred in September of 2024 and resulted in the selection of 78 eligible recipients from a pool of 454 applications. Pursuant to the initial authorizing law, the program was to terminate when the funds allocated by Legislature were fully expended or by December 31, 2024, whichever occurred first. However, additional funding was approved by the 131st Legislature ($2.65 million in additional federal funds and $2 million in additional state funds). In January of
2024, FAME received an additional $2,602,115.96 from the state via a provision in the
enacted biennial budget stipulating that any unused money from a certain account at

DPFR would be sent to FAME for use with this program. (Public Law 2023, c.3, Part C
included language directing that any remaining available balance from the Small Business Health Insurance Premium Support Program be transferred to the Maine Health
Care Provider Loan Repayment Fund at FAME).
There is approximately $350,000 in remaining program funds. A third application
A
cycle opened on February 1. Without additional funding, we expect that third cycle to
absorb the remaining program funds. $1 million in ongoing funding would translate into approximately 15-18 awards annually.
The program has proven to be popular and is helping to meet Maine's health care workforce needs. The prioritization of professions awarded is based on the following factors: (1) access to health care for the population where the applicant practices or intends to practice, such as number of vacancies within a local provider system, timeliness of appointments, and whether they or their employer accepts Medicaid; (2) monthly student debt obligation payment as a percentage of gross monthly income; (3) the need for specific health care practitioners in a given employment region; and (4) the workforce needs of Maine health care providers, with special emphasis on the
following occupations:
[I Nurses 1] Occupational Therapists El Certified Occupational Therapy Assistants Kl Physical Therapists El Speech Therapists III Behavioral Health Care Workers El Licensed Clinical Social Workers including, but not limited to, applied Behavioral Analysts and Board-Certified Behavior Analysts, and Licensed Clinical Professional Counselors El Dental Hygienists
U Dental Therapists U Medical Assistants U Pharmacists
IIlHealth Care Technicians, including, but not limited to, Respiratory Therapists,
Surgical Technicians, and Imaging Technicians such as MRI Technicians and
Ultra Sonographers
We fully recognize and are sensitive to the challenging budgetary situation facing
the Administration and this Legislature, but the conversation regarding the positive impact of this program, to both participating students and the communities they serve, as well as the sustainability of this program, is an important one to have nonetheless.
Thank you for your consideration of the bill. I will be happy to answer any questions you have.
